correctness.rationale: Two vertices generate H precisely when their projected subspaces span the symplectic four-space. Each fiber has one full preimage and, only for an isotropic image U, q^{dim U} graphs of functionals. There are N=(q+1)(q²+1) lines, Lagrangian planes, and hyperplanes, and q²(q²+1) nonisotropic planes. A projected line meets q³ hyperplane neighbors. A plane has q³+q² hyperplane neighbors and q⁴ complementary planes, with the extra isotropic-fiber lift count obtained from symmetric two-by-two matrices for Lagrangian U or determinant −1 matrices for nonisotropic U. Those counts, q³ and q(q²−1), respectively, hold also in characteristic two. For hyperplanes the incidence count of outside Lagrangian planes is q²(q+1); adding their extra lifts to the ordinary outside-subspace counts gives the stated hyperplane degree. The five entries strictly increase in the order displayed. Direct polynomial expansion of the multiplicity sum and factorization of the degree sum checked both total counts. All hyperplanes form a clique and coloring a projected subspace by any hyperplane containing it gives a proper N-coloring. For any two nonzero images a functional outside both annihilators exists and its kernel is adjacent to both if they are not already adjacent; within a line fiber there is a nonadjacent pair. This proves diameter two after deleting the center.
residual_risks: The independent enumeration is over F₂ only. The all-field result relies on the symbolic proof, not an extrapolation of finite counts.

evidence: The Frattini quotient theorem gives spanning-adjacency via independent fibers off the Frattini subalgebra. For H, the Frattini equals the central line since the maximal subalgebras are the preimages of all projected hyperplanes.
